review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked at the scoped simp lemmas (coe_toRoot, coe_ofRoot, coe_β, coe_β_symm, coe_ρT_apply, coe_jV) and at the rfl-style `*_apply` lemmas that are used only through `rw`. The scoped simp lemmas look consistently oriented and I saw no competing pairs or cycle risk among them. The two findings are modest: missing canonical simp lemmas whose analogues in the same file are already simp. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour. Whether adding the attribute is safe depends on downstream `simp` calls elsewhere, which I did not check. I did not treat the large `attribute [-simp]` header as a defect.

findings.excerpt: tT p J t x = t • x := Subtype.ext rfl
findings.problem: `tT p J t x = t • x` is the canonical, simplest form of the Hecke action on the transported Tate module. It is not marked simp, although `coe_ρT_apply` (the analogous Galois-action lemma) is `@[scoped simp]`. The same-LHS lemma `tT_apply'` gives an unfolded form through `β.symm`/`TateModule.rep`, so a user cannot tell which one is the intended normal form. The only use, `hT`, picks the rewrite by hand: `rw [TM_apply, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, tT_apply]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `tT_apply` as `@[scoped simp]` so `tT p J t x` normalises to `t • x`. Leave `tT_apply'` as a non-simp unfolding lemma and say in a comment that it is the unfolding direction. Alternatively add `tT_apply` to the `simp only` sets of downstream proofs that mention `tT`.
findings.benefit: The Hecke operator on the transported module reduces to the module action (`t • x`) under `simp`, as the Galois action already does via `coe_ρT_apply`. The two same-LHS lemmas no longer look interchangeable. Proofs like `hT` and `hquad_jZero`/`quadratic_of_root` need less manual rewriting.

findings.problem: `coe_ρres` says the coercion of `ρres … σ v` is `ρA … σ v`. It is the coe-of-apply lemma for `ρres`, like `coe_jV` and `coe_ρT_apply`, which are `@[scoped simp]`. But it is a plain `rfl` theorem, and `ρres` is a bundled def with no simp interface. Consequently `ρres`'s own `map_one'` and `map_mul'` are proved with manual `show … ; rw [map_one]; rfl`, and `jmap_ρres` needs an explicit `rw [coe_ρres, jmap_ρA]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coe_ρres` as `@[scoped simp]` (its LHS is a coercion of an application, so it terminates). Also consider making `jmap_ρA` and `jmap_ρres` simp lemmas. Then the `show … rfl` steps in `ρres.map_one'`/`map_mul'` and `ram_latt` can use `simp`, or at least `rw [coe_ρres]`.
findings.benefit: Subtype-ext goals about `ρres` normalise to statements about `ρA` and the base-changed `FA` without `show` or `rfl`. This matches how `latt` and `jV` are handled (`coe_jV`).
